title: Prime-to-ell profinite linear monodromy has finite image
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a norm-topological finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $H$ be a profinite group all of whose finite continuous quotient groups have order prime to $\ell$. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space and let $\rho:H\to\operatorname{GL}_E(M)$ be a representation such that $H\times M\to M$ is continuous. Then $\rho(H)$ is finite and has order prime to $\ell$. The zero-dimensional vector space is allowed.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, pp. 2-3, stable lattice argument; agent corollary using the filtration of the principal congruence subgroup by additive residue-field matrices.

proof.text: If $M=0$, its only automorphism is the identity, so the image has order $1$. Otherwise put $r=\dim_E M$. Apply [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice] with $G=H$ and $V=M$: a profinite group is compact and the action is jointly continuous by hypothesis. Obtain a stable free $\mathcal O_E$-lattice $\Lambda$ of rank $r$ spanning $M$, with continuous restricted action and its maximal-ideal-adic topology equal to the subspace topology. Choose a basis of $\Lambda$. It is an $E$-basis of $M$: its $r$ vectors span a space of dimension $r$. In this basis write $A(h)\in\operatorname{GL}_r(\mathcal O_E)$ for the action; stability for $h$ and $h^{-1}$ supplies both an integral matrix and an integral inverse.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second bullet, p. 3: choose a stable lattice.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal O=\mathcal O_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, and $A_n=\mathcal O/\pi^n\mathcal O$ for $n\geq1$, with the coefficient notation of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. The rings $A_n$ are finite by [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients], applied to the valuation ring and uniformizer supplied by that coefficient datum. Reduction of the matrices defines $\rho_n:H\to\operatorname{GL}_r(A_n)$; put $Q_n=\rho_n(H)$ and $K_n=\ker\rho_n$. Each $Q_n$ is finite because its matrices have finitely many entries in a finite ring. Moreover $\rho_n$ is continuous for the discrete topology: for each basis vector $e_j$, $h\mapsto\rho(h)e_j$ is continuous into $\Lambda$ by [lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice], and reduction modulo $\pi^n\Lambda$ has open fibres in the adic topology. Finitely many such evaluations determine the reduced matrix. Thus $H\to Q_n$ is a continuous surjective homomorphism to a finite group, so $\gcd(|Q_n|,\ell)=1$ by the hypothesis on $H$.

source.place: Proposition 1.1.9, second and third bullets, p. 3; elementary construction of finite continuous reduction images.

proof.text: For every $n\geq1$ and matrix $B$ over $\mathcal O$, repeated multiplication gives $(I+\pi^nB)^m\equiv I+m\pi^nB\pmod{\pi^{n+1}}$ for all integers $m\geq0$: the base $m=0$ is immediate, and the induction step multiplies by $I+\pi^nB$, whose extra product term is divisible by $\pi^{2n}$, hence by $\pi^{n+1}$. By [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $|\ell|_E=|\ell|_\ell=\ell^{-1}<1$, so $\ell\in\mathfrak m_E=\pi\mathcal O$. Taking $m=\ell$ gives $(I+\pi^nB)^\ell\equiv I\pmod{\pi^{n+1}}$. This calculation works also at $\ell=2$ and for ramified $E$.

source.place: Agent expansion after Proposition 1.1.9: first-order matrix congruence calculation (not asserted in the notes).

proof.text: We prove $K_1=K_n$ by induction on $n\geq1$. The base $n=1$ is equality. Suppose $K_1=K_n$ and take $h\in K_1$. Since $h\in K_n$, every entry of $A(h)-I$ is divisible by $\pi^n$, so $A(h)=I+\pi^nB$ for a matrix $B$ over $\mathcal O$. The previous calculation implies $\rho_{n+1}(h)^\ell=1$ in $Q_{n+1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-matrix-group-coprime-power] to $R=A_{n+1}$, $G=Q_{n+1}$ and exponent $\ell$; the needed coprimality was established in Step 2. Its power map is injective and sends $1$ to $1$, so $\rho_{n+1}(h)=1$. This proves $K_1\subseteq K_{n+1}$; the reverse inclusion follows by reduction modulo $\pi$. This completes the induction.

source.place: Agent corollary to Proposition 1.1.9: induction on congruence depth using the Mathlib coprime-power bijection.

proof.text: If $h\in K_1$, Step 4 gives $A(h)-I\in\pi^nM_r(\mathcal O)$ for every $n\geq1$. For any entry $a$ of this difference, $a\in\pi^n\mathcal O$ implies $|a|_E\leq|\pi|_E^n$. Here $0<|\pi|_E<1$ by [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], so the right side tends to zero and $a=0$. Thus $A(h)=I$, which implies $\rho(h)=1$ since $\Lambda$ spans $M$. Conversely $\rho(h)=1$ implies $h\in K_1$. Therefore $\ker\rho=K_1$. The rule $\rho(h)\mapsto\rho_1(h)$ is consequently a well-defined bijective group homomorphism $\rho(H)\to Q_1$: equality of reductions is equivalent to $h_2^{-1}h_1\in K_1=\ker\rho$. Its target is finite and has order prime to $\ell$ by Step 2, proving both assertions.

source.place: Agent expansion after Proposition 1.1.9: separatedness of the lattice and identification with the first finite reduction image.
